note: "einen Kulturschock erleben" — the disorientation of encountering an unfamiliar culture, especially early after a move.

examples.de: Nach dem Umzug erlebte sie einen echten Kulturschock.
examples.en: After the move, she experienced real culture shock.

note: an oversimplified, fixed idea about a group — the cognitive starting point B2 Unit 16's das Vorurteil often builds on.

examples.de: Stereotype über andere Kulturen halten sich oft hartnäckig.
examples.en: Stereotypes about other cultures are often persistent.

note: close to das Stereotyp but usually lighter and more about a tired, overused idea than a harmful judgment.

examples.de: Der Film bedient viele Klischees über das Reisen.
examples.en: The film plays into many clichés about travel.

note: "unterschiedliche Kommunikationsstile aufeinandertreffen" — how someone typically expresses themselves, which can vary sharply between cultures.

examples.de: Der Kommunikationsstil unterscheidet sich stark zwischen den beiden Ländern.
examples.en: Communication style differs greatly between the two countries.

note: saying what you mean plainly and explicitly — often associated (rightly or not) with German communication norms.

examples.de: Direkte Kommunikation wird in manchen Kulturen als unhöflich empfunden.
examples.en: Direct communication is perceived as impolite in some cultures.

note: relying on context, hints, and tone rather than explicit statements — the natural counterpart to direkte Kommunikation.

examples.de: Indirekte Kommunikation erfordert, zwischen den Zeilen zu lesen.
examples.en: Indirect communication requires reading between the lines.

note: a culture where meaning relies heavily on shared context and nonverbal cues, not just spoken words — a concept from intercultural-communication studies.

examples.de: In einer Hochkontextkultur sagt oft der Kontext mehr als die Worte selbst.
examples.en: In a high-context culture, the context often says more than the words themselves.

note: the natural counterpart — a culture where communication relies mainly on explicit, spoken content rather than shared context.

examples.de: Niedrigkontextkulturen legen großen Wert auf klare, explizite Aussagen.
examples.en: Low-context cultures place great value on clear, explicit statements.

english: to put your foot in it, commit a cultural faux pas
note: a vivid, very common idiom — literally "to step into the grease pot."

examples.de: Bei seiner ersten Geschäftsreise trat er gleich mehrmals ins Fettnäpfchen.
examples.en: On his first business trip, he put his foot in it several times.

note: an English loanword — how much small talk is expected (or even welcome) before getting to business varies enormously by culture.

examples.de: In manchen Ländern gehört ausführlicher Small Talk einfach dazu.
examples.en: In some countries, extensive small talk is simply expected.

note: handshake, bow, cheek kiss, or something else entirely — one of the first cultural differences most people notice.

examples.de: Das Begrüßungsritual unterscheidet sich von Land zu Land erheblich.
examples.en: The greeting ritual differs considerably from country to country.

note: "die Körpersprache lesen/deuten" — gestures and posture that can carry very different meanings across cultures.

examples.de: Ein Nicken bedeutet nicht in jeder Kultur dasselbe — Körpersprache muss man lernen wie eine Sprache.
examples.en: A nod doesn't mean the same thing in every culture — body language has to be learned like a language.

note: "Blickkontakt halten/vermeiden" — read as confidence in some cultures, and as disrespect in others.

examples.de: Zu viel Blickkontakt wird nicht überall als respektvoll empfunden.
examples.en: Too much eye contact isn't seen as respectful everywhere.

english: polite form, polite register (e.g. Sie vs. du)
note: German's own famous example — choosing the wrong Höflichkeitsform is a classic way to step ins Fettnäpfchen.

examples.de: Die richtige Höflichkeitsform zu wählen, ist für Deutschlernende oft eine Herausforderung.
examples.en: Choosing the correct polite form is often a challenge for German learners.

english: change of perspective, putting yourself in someone else's shoes
note: "einen Perspektivwechsel vollziehen" — deliberately trying to see a situation the way someone from a different background would.

examples.de: Ein bewusster Perspektivwechsel hilft, Missverständnisse zu vermeiden.
examples.en: A deliberate change of perspective helps avoid misunderstandings.

note: "Empathie zeigen" — the emotional counterpart to the more cognitive der Perspektivwechsel.

examples.de: Empathie ist eine Grundvoraussetzung für gelungene interkulturelle Kommunikation.
examples.en: Empathy is a basic requirement for successful intercultural communication.

english: understanding the unfamiliar/foreign (a specific pedagogical concept)
note: a term from intercultural-education theory — genuinely understanding another perspective from the inside, not just tolerating it from the outside.

examples.de: Fremdverstehen bedeutet mehr als bloße Toleranz gegenüber anderen Kulturen.
examples.en: Understanding the unfamiliar means more than mere tolerance of other cultures.

note: a category used in intercultural research (like individualism vs. collectivism) to compare cultures systematically.

examples.de: Individualismus und Kollektivismus gelten als zentrale Kulturdimensionen.
examples.en: Individualism and collectivism are considered central cultural dimensions.

note: "im internationalen Kulturvergleich" — systematically comparing practices or values between cultures.

examples.de: Im Kulturvergleich zeigen sich deutliche Unterschiede im Umgang mit Zeit.
examples.en: Cross-cultural comparison shows clear differences in how time is handled.

note: "sich an eine neue Kultur anpassen" — the ongoing process of adjusting your own behaviour in a new cultural setting.

examples.de: Die Anpassung an eine neue Kultur braucht Zeit und Geduld.
examples.en: Adapting to a new culture takes time and patience.

note: "vorurteilsfrei an etwas herangehen" — the goal this whole unit points toward, and the opposite of B2 Unit 16's das Vorurteil.

examples.de: Sie versucht, jeder neuen Kultur möglichst vorurteilsfrei zu begegnen.
examples.en: She tries to approach every new culture as free of prejudice as possible.

note: how negotiation actually happens in a given culture — pace, directness, the role of relationship-building — relevant to B2 Unit 11's der Verhandlungsgeschick in an international setting.

examples.de: Die Verhandlungskultur unterscheidet sich stark zwischen den beiden Geschäftspartnern.
examples.en: Negotiation culture differs greatly between the two business partners.

english: monochronic time orientation (doing one thing at a time, on schedule)
note: a concept from intercultural studies — schedules and punctuality treated as fixed and sequential, contrasted with polychrones Zeitverständnis.

examples.de: Ein monochrones Zeitverständnis legt großen Wert auf Pünktlichkeit und feste Termine.
examples.en: A monochronic time orientation places great value on punctuality and fixed appointments.

english: polychronic time orientation (flexible, several things at once)
note: the counterpart — time treated more flexibly, with relationships and circumstances taking priority over a fixed schedule.

examples.de: Bei einem polychronen Zeitverständnis sind mehrere gleichzeitige Termine keine Seltenheit.
examples.en: With a polychronic time orientation, several simultaneous appointments aren't unusual.

note: "jemandem Gastfreundschaft entgegenbringen" — norms around welcoming guests vary widely and are a common source of cross-cultural admiration or friction.

examples.de: Die Gastfreundschaft der Familie beeindruckte sie sehr.
examples.en: The family's hospitality impressed her greatly.

note: "ein Tabuthema ansprechen" — topics considered acceptable in casual conversation vary sharply between cultures (money, age, religion, politics...).

examples.de: Über das Gehalt zu sprechen, gilt in Deutschland fast als Tabuthema.
examples.en: Talking about salary is considered almost a taboo subject in Germany.

english: code-switching (switching language or register depending on context)
note: "zwischen zwei Sprachen/Registern wechseln" — common among multilingual speakers and bicultural people moving between social contexts.

examples.de: Viele Mehrsprachige beherrschen den Codewechsel ganz selbstverständlich.
examples.en: Many multilingual people switch codes quite naturally.

german: Rückblick: drei Wege zur interkulturellen Kompetenz
english: review — three earlier angles on intercultural competence
note: B2 Unit 11 introduced interkulturelle Kompetenz as a workplace skill; Unit 16 covered migration policy and contested cultural-debate terms; Unit 21 covered art's role in cultural representation. This unit gives you the actual mechanics of communication itself — styles, rituals, and the concepts intercultural researchers use to compare cultures.

examples.de: Erst die Kompetenz, dann die Politik, dann die Kunst — und jetzt das Gespräch selbst.
examples.en: First the competence, then the policy, then the art — and now the conversation itself.
